item.title: Foreign ministers of Egypt, Pakistan discuss regional developments ahead of OIC meet
item.description:
Foreign ministers of Egypt, Pakistan discuss regional developments ahead of OIC meet

Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty has said that he discussed regional developments with his Pakistani counterpart, Mohammad Ishaq Dar, in a phone call.

In a post on X, Abdelatty said they discussed ways to de-escalate regional tensions and enhance joint coordination ahead of an upcoming meeting of Organisation of Islamic Cooperation foreign ministers scheduled to be hosted in Baghdad on 17-18 October.

item.title: Attacks on Saudi Arabia could impact people 'everywhere', IMF chief says
item.description:
Attacks on Saudi Arabia could impact people 'everywhere', IMF chief says

International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said that recent attacks on Saudi Arabia could impact people "everywhere", as energy costs rise globally and multiple conflicts rage in the crude-rich region.

"The Saudi economy is important for the region and the world, and in that sense, these developments have potentially negative spillovers for everybody, everywhere," Georgieva said at a news conference during the Annual Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank in Bangkok, according to AFP.

item.title: Ahead of US polls, Iran shifts Hormuz attack tactics, report says
item.description:
Ahead of US polls, Iran shifts Hormuz attack tactics, report says

Iran is deploying new tactics to target ships sailing through the Strait of Hormuz as it seeks to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters.

The two officials declined to provide details of the new strategy, but one said that Iran had started using different offensive tactics against vessels it considered in violation of its restrictions about 10 days ago, adding that this had led to an increase in attacks on such ships.

The strategy included a change in the type as well as the pace of attacks, with one goal being to influence the outcome of the US vote, they said.

"The aim is to frustrate efforts by the United States and its allies to bring down global oil prices," one of the two officials said.

The decision to adopt the new strategy had been taken at the highest levels of Iran’s leadership and was fully coordinated across the country’s ruling system, the officials said.

A US military official, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed that Iran had changed tactics in one significant way: after the US destroyed much of Iran’s radar capabilities, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had started using unarmed spotters in small boats to identify potential targets, including US naval vessels, the official said.

In recent days, attacks on commercial ships still sailing through the strait have surged to their highest level since the war began, according to independent data.

Report by Reuters

item.title: Israeli forces raid Ramallah, shut down offices of several organizations
item.description: Israeli forces raided the city of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank on Tuesday, shutting down the offices of several organizations, Anadolu reports. During the raid, Israeli soldiers reportedly confiscated furniture and other belongings from the offices. Israeli army raids and attacks by occupiers against Palestinians and their property have intensified across the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, since the start of Israel’s war on Gaza in October 2023. Palestinians say illegal settlement expansion and attacks threaten the possibility of establishing an independent Palestinian state in line with relevant international resolutions. item.description: A senior commander of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy threatened to sink US warships on Tuesday if they approach the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran’s state news agency IRNA. “We are waiting for American warships to approach the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz so that we can sink them,” Rear Adm. item.title: UN experts urge food agency to uphold human rights amid concerns about Gaza-related work
item.description: UN experts on Tuesday urged the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) to uphold human rights and protect staff following concerns about the treatment of officials who worked on food insecurity and starvation in the Gaza Strip, Anadolu reports. The experts expressed concern about remarks by the FAO director-general that appeared to link the departure of senior officials to their engagement with human rights issues. “Human rights principles are not peripheral to the FAO’s mandate; they are central to it,” said the experts. They said documenting starvation in Gaza was consistent with the agency’s mandate to combat hunger and did not constitute a breach of impartiality. item.title: If You Cannot Say Genocide: Essays on Conscience and Witness
item.description: “What task is left to art when words are turned into weapons?” Yahia Lababidi’s If you Cannot Say Genocide: Essays of Conscience and Witness explores the depth of this question impressed upon the reader in the preface. For the author, who is a Muslim of Palestinian descent, the question is pondered from a position of distance as an “inheritor of family dispossession”.  Written between 2023 and 2026, this collection of essays leans upon memory, literature, experiences, observation and reflection, through which disillusion exposes reality. While there is no chronology in Lababidi’s reflections, the preoccupation with words and meaning is persistent.
